date_note: SANS diary published Nov 16; picked up Nov 18.
title: SANS honeypots see scans for chained LiteLLM and Starlette flaws (CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710)
summary: SANS ISC honeypots recorded requests to /mcp-rest/test/tools/list attempting to chain CVE-2026-42271 in LiteLLM with CVE-2026-48710 in Starlette for unauthenticated remote code execution. Starlette before 1.0.1 does not validate the Host header. SANS cites a Horizon3.ai write-up on the chain and says exploitation was reported in July. Whether any attempts succeeded is not stated.
plain: SANS researchers saw probing of LiteLLM servers using two chained flaws that could let attackers run code without logging in. SANS does not say whether any attempt succeeded.
exec: SANS says honeypots saw scanning for this chain, and a Horizon3.ai write-up on it exists.
action: SANS advises defending against the underlying vulnerability, validating hostnames, reducing attack surface and patching; Starlette 1.0.1 is the version that validates the Host header. The page gives no LiteLLM fix version.

key_findings: Honeypots saw requests aimed at chaining CVE-2026-42271 (LiteLLM) with CVE-2026-48710 (Starlette).
